sections.title: Clinical Definition
sections.content: Shock: Circulatory failure resulting in inadequate organ perfusion. (Source: Waleed Badr, FRCS INTERNAL & EMERGENCY MEDICINE FOR FRCS (GLASG) EXAM 2016)

sections.title: The Seven Primary Etiologies of Shock

branches: 1) Cardiogenic: Pump failure or 2ry to PE, tension pneumothorax & cardiac tamponade (Obstructive Shock).
2) Hypovolaemic: Loss of blood volume (Trauma, Ruptured Aneurysm, Ectopic Pregnancy, Vomiting/GIT obstruction, Diarrhea/Cholera, Burns, Heat Exhaustion).
4) Neurogenic: Nervous system injury (e.g., post spinal surgery).
7) Endocrine Failure: Addison’s disease or Hypothyroidism.

rows: Temp: Commonly hypothermia. Heart Rate: Commonly tachycardia >100 bpm. BP: Early rise (COP increase), then rapid fall (hypotension). Resp Rate: Increase (compensatory tachypnea to remove CO2/acid).
Early: Personality change, restlessness. Late: Confusion, ultimately coma.
Chest pain. Profound acidosis and abnormal heart rhythms (cardiac dysrhythmias) are prevalent and potentially fatal.
Due to blood shunting. Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, GIT bleeding with black/tarry stool (melena).
Cold, pale, clammy & cyanosed (if extreme low blood O2 content).

sections.title: General Management Protocol
content: CRITICAL: If BP unrecordable, call the cardiac arrest team.
1. Call for help + Position patient on hard surface with raised legs.
2. A (Airway): Ensure patent airway (remove obstruction, chin elevation, head tilt) & adequate ventilation.
3. B (Breathing): Administer O2 100%.
4. C (Circulation): IV access x2 wide bore (get help if this takes > 2 min).
5. Identify & treat underlying cause: Check abdomen for trauma/aneurysm, GIT bleeding/melena. If unclear, treat as Hypovolaemic (most common).
6. Consider: Arterial line, central venous line & Foley's catheter.
7. Fluids: Infuse crystalloids fast to raise BP (unless cardiogenic). Aim for urine flow > 30 mL/h. Titrate by BP, CVP & output.
8. NB: Do not overload fluids in Cardiogenic shock (exclude PE & RV infarct first).
9. Monitor: Pulse, BP, temp, respiration, and peripheral perfusion.
10. Investigations: FBC, U&E, ABG, glucose, cross matching, ECG.

sections.title: Cardiogenic Shock Management
content: Characterized by cold & clammy patient; High mortality.
Can occur suddenly or after worsening heart failure.
Requires senior physician help for diagnosis & treatment.
Causes: MI, myocarditis, myocardial depression (drugs, hypoxia, acidosis, sepsis), endocarditis, arrhythmias, or 2ry to tamponade/pneumothorax/PE.
MI Management: Prompt thrombolysis or acute angioplasty. Manage in CCU/ICU.
Medication: Morphine (2.5 – 5 mg IV) for pain/anxiety.
Monitoring: ECG (hourly until diagnosed), enzymes/troponins, U&E, CXR, Echo, ABG, CVP, urine output.
Swan-Ganz Catheter: Assess PCWP and cardiac output.
PCWP < 15 mm Hg: Plasma expanders (100 mL every 15 min IV); aim for 15 – 20 mm Hg.
PCWP > 15 mm Hg: +ve inotropes (Dopamine or Dobutamine 2.5 – 10 ug/kg/min IVI); aim for systolic BP > 80 mm Hg.
Surgical: Consider surgery for valvular lesions; treat reversible causes like MI/PE.

sections.title: Cardiac Tamponade Essentials
content: Definition: Pericardial fluid collection -> High intrapericardial pressure -> Heart cannot fill -> Pumping stops.
Causes: Trauma, Lung/Breast Cancer, Pericarditis, MI.
Beck’s Triad: Low BP, High JVP, Muffled heart sounds.
Kussmaul’s sign: JVP increases on inspiration.
Pulsus paradoxus: Pulse fades on inspiration.
ECG: Electrical alternans.
CXR: Globular heart, Lt. heart border convex/straight, Rt. costophrenic angle < 90°.
Echo: Diagnostic.
Treatment: Prompt pericardiocentesis (requires senior help/luck).
Await surgery/procedure: O2, ECG monitor, IVI, Group & Save blood.
Surgical roles: CABG, ventricular repair, or pericardial window.

rows: Treat underlying cause (control hemorrhage, urgent laparotomy/thoracotomy). Fluid: Saline 0.9% or colloid initially. If bleeding: Cross matched blood or Group O Rh -ve via large bore cannula. Titrate against BP, CVP, urine. Correct electrolytes/acidosis.

Endotoxin-induced vasodilatation. Presentation: Warm and well-perfused with bounding pulse (may lack fever/high WCC). Treatment: Antibiotics after blood culture (e.g., IV Cefuroxime 1.5g/8h or Gentamycin + Antipseudomonal). Fluids: Colloid/Crystalloid IVI. Monitor: ICU (CVP and PAWP).

content.explanation: Type 1 IgE-mediated hypersensitivity. Histamine/mediator release from mast cells -> increased vascular permeability, vasodilatation & respiratory smooth muscle contraction.

sections.title: Anaphylaxis: Clinical Features & Causes
content: Causes: Penicillin, Radiology contrast (FA), Stings, Foods (strawberries, eggs, fish).
Anaphylactoid: Direct mediator release without antibodies (drug-related).
Features: Allergy history, Itching, Sweating, Erythema, Urticaria.
Systemic Signs: Tachycardia, Hypotension, Wheezing, Laryngeal obstruction (edema), Apnea, Cyanosis.
Other: Vomiting, Diarrhea, Urinary incontinence, Syncope.

sections.title: Anaphylaxis Emergency Treatment
content: 1. Remove cause, raise feet, call for help.
2. ABC: Airway, 100% O2, Secure IV access.
3. Adrenaline: 0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1:1000) IM. Repeat every 5 min guided by BP/Pulse/Respiration until better.
4. Antihistamine: Chlorpheniramine 10 mg IV (repeat every 6h if urticaria persists).
5. Hydrocortisone: 200 mg IV.
6. If Hypotensive: IVI 0.9% saline 500 ml over 15 min (up to 2L may be needed).
7. If Bronchospasm: Aminophylline & nebulized Salbutamol 2.5 mg.
8. If Laryngeal Edema Worsens (Stridor): Refer to ICU, Intubation/Ventilation.
9. Severe/No Pulse Case: IV Adrenaline (1 mL of 1:10,000 solution per minute). Stop at response.
10. Discharge: Only after 48hrs due to risk of Biphasic Reaction.

sections.title: Prophylaxis & Prevention
content: Detailed history of atopy, drug allergy, or stings.
Identify Family H/O anaphylaxis (AD inheritance).
Skin-prick tests for specific IgE to identify allergens.
Emergency tray: Ambu bag, mask, laryngoscope, ET tube, O2, Meds (Adrenaline, hydrocortisone, antihistaminics, aminophylline, IV glucose).
Staff training for emergencies.
Suggest Medic-alert bracelet.
Teach self-injected adrenaline techniques.

rows: Cause: Generalized vasodilatation. Picture: Bradycardia & hypotension. Treatment: Raise legs, IVI fluids, Atropine 1mg IV & Hydrocortisone 200mg IV.
Treatment: Tepid sponging and fanning. Avoid ice/immersion. IVI 0.9% saline ± Hydrocortisone 100mg IV. Chlorpromazine 25mg IM (stops shivering). Stop cooling at core temp < 39°C.
